facts.fact: George C. Thomas Jr. and William P. Bell, opened 1 January 1930, in the foothills behind the campus.
The Stanford Dish, a 150 ft radio telescope built in 1961, stands in the Stanford foothills.

current.subject: An arcade inspired by the Main Quad, in a round badge.
current.keep: The sandstone arcade and red tile roof.
current.weaknesses: The badge's sky, grass and flag crowd the arches.

concepts.name: The Arcade
concepts.rationale: Three Romanesque arches in buff sandstone under a red tile roof: the architecture alone, chunky and clear.
concepts.symbolism: A campus landmark beside the course.
concepts.tradeoffs: The university's architecture, not the course's.

concepts.name: The Dish
concepts.rationale: The radio telescope on a golden foothill.
concepts.symbolism: Science in the foothills the course shares.
concepts.strengths: Unexpected and memorable; clear of university marks.
concepts.tradeoffs: Visibility from specific holes isn't verified.

recommendation: Concept 2. The Dish is ownable in golf and clear of the university's trademarks.
